title: Halting in the tail phase
statement: Let $a,b,f,B$ be natural numbers, let $m$ be a Boolean value, let $o$ be a function assigning a Boolean value to each index in ${0,1,2,3,4}$ and each finite Boolean word, and let $y$ be a finite Boolean word. For any fifteen-register configuration $st$ whose register values are all at most $B$, the abstract program started in its tail phase with register values given by $st$ and no result halts with answer $tailAns(m,st.i)$; every configuration strictly before halting satisfies the program guard.
hypotheses_covered: $o$ assigns Boolean values to indices in ${0,1,2,3,4}$ and finite Boolean words
every register value of $st$ is at most $B$
replaced:
Let $a,b,f,B$ be natural numbers, let $m$ be a Boolean value, let $o$ assign a Boolean
answer to each of five possible indices and each Boolean string, and let $y$ be a
Boolean string. For every fifteen-register configuration $st$ whose register values are
all at most $B$, the abstract program started at its tail instruction with register
values given by $st$ and no result halts with answer determined by $st.i$: the answer is
true when $st.i=1$ or $st.i\ge 3$, and is $m$ otherwise; every configuration before
halting satisfies the program guard.
